title: Tenancy models (silo, pool, and bridge)
hook: SaaS tenancy models describe how you isolate customers. Silo dedicates resources per tenant; pool shares infrastructure with logical isolation; bridge mixes both — pooled compute with siloed data or premium tiers on dedicated stacks.

blocks.text: Silo model: separate database, compute, or account per tenant — maximum isolation, highest cost. Pool model: shared application and database with tenant_id column partitioning — best economies of scale. Bridge model: pooled control plane with tiered data isolation — free tier pooled, enterprise silo. AWS SaaS Lens maps these to Well-Architected tradeoffs.

entries.plainDefinition: Mix pooled and silo by tier

blocks.text: Top SaaS architecture interview question: "how do you isolate tenants?" Wrong answer ignores blast radius and cost. Right answer names model, tradeoffs, and migration path between tiers.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: silo = dedicated, pool = shared with logical isolation, bridge = tiered mix.

items.title: Classify tenant tiers
items.body: Free/starter → pool. Enterprise/regulated → silo or bridge.

snippet.label: Silo — dedicated stack per tenant
snippet.code:
Resources:
  TenantDb:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      DBInstanceIdentifier: !Sub tenant-${TenantId}-db
      DBInstanceClass: db.r6g.large
snippet.explanation: CloudFormation per-tenant stack for silo enterprise tier.

snippet.label: Repository always scopes tenant
snippet.explanation: Missing tenant_id in query is cross-tenant data leak — top SaaS bug.

blocks.title: Cloud vs app patterns
rows: Hard cutover from shared to dedicated

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Pool model without tenant_id on every table and query. Silo for all customers on day one — burn rate kills startup. No migration path from pool to silo.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: integration tests that attempt cross-tenant access must fail; per-tier cost attribution; silo provisioning time SLA for enterprise onboarding.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: One model for all tiers without tradeoff discussion — rejected. Strong answer: pool for scale, silo for enterprise, bridge for tiered product.

interviewTakeaways: Silo = dedicated, pool = shared logical isolation, bridge = tiered mix.
Pool requires tenant_id on every query — no exceptions.
Bridge aligns isolation with pricing tiers.
60s: Pool for scale and cost. Silo for compliance and blast radius. Bridge tiers free pooled to enterprise silo. SaaS Lens framework.
Follow-up: how migrate tenant from pool to silo?
commonPitfalls: Missing tenant_id filter — cross-tenant data leak, instant rejection.
Strong answer: middleware tenant context, composite keys, integration tests for isolation.
Silo everything day one — unsustainable burn.
